newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CHELSEA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF CHELSEA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of players most likely to play for Chelsea against Manchester United in an English premier league match at Stamford Bridge on Saturday:

Kevin Hitchcock (goalkeeper) age 34. Stepped into the Chelsea first team for an F.A. Cup tie against Newcastle last season and saved two penalties in a dramatic shoot-out. Since then has been a regular after seven seasons as understudy to former England squad keeper Dave Beasant and Russian Dmitry Kharin. Could lose his place if reports that Gullit is set to sign either AC Milan's Sebastiano Rossi or Ipswich youngster Richard Wright prove correct.

Scott Minto (defender/midfielder) 25. Natural wing-back whose career at Chelsea has been blighted by injury since his arrival from first division Charlton. Nevertheless, has struck up a fluid partnership with Italy's Roberto di Matteo on the left flank this season.

Steve Clark (defender) 33. Scottish international whose days in the first team looked numbered when Chelsea signed right-back Dan Petrescu. Proved his adaptabilty by moving across to the left where he has enjoyed one of the finest of his 10 seasons at Stamford Bridge.

Franck Leboeuf (defender) 29. Balding centre-back who joined from Strasbourg after last year's European championship when he consolidated his place in the French national side. The organiser in the Chelsea back line. Dangerous coming forward too.
Frank Sinclair (defender) 25. Burly full-back who has learned a lot from playing alongside Leboeuf and Clarke this year. Sent off in the corresponding fixture against United last season.

Dan Petrescu (defender/midfielder) 29. Classy right-sided wing-back signed by Glenn Hoddle last season. Gets forward at every opportunity and uses space intelligently. An automatic choice for Romania, for whom he has been capped over 50 times.

Roberto di Matteo (midfielder) 26. Signed from Lazio after a successful European championship for Italy last June. Has scored a number of superb goals from the edge of the box since then, the latest against Leicester last Sunday. Born in Switzerland, turned down an offer to play for the Swiss national side. Has said his dream is to have five children.

Eddie Newton (midfielder) 25. Hard tackler who plays the holding role in Chelsea's midfield allowing di Matteo and Dennis Wise to sweep forward. Broke his right shin last season but is back in form now.

Ruud Gullit (midfielder) 34. Player-manager who has transformed Chelsea since arrival from Italy, bringing half of serie A to west London in his wake. Still a wonderful talent on the increasingly rare occasions he plays. Will start on the bench on Saturday but could come on later to tease the United midfield. Enjoying a blossoming career as an articulate television soccer pundit.

Dennis Wise (midfielder) 30. Dynamic club captain always in the thick of things. Born within a couple of miles of "the Bridge". Makes up for his lack of height (167 cm) by packing a great right-foot strike. On the fringes of the England squad last season.

Craig Burley (midfielder) 25. Hard-working Scottish international. Will want to forget his role in Chelsea's 2-1 F.A. Cup semifinal defeat against United last season. His miscued backpass set up David Beckham to score the winner.

Mark Hughes (forward) 33. Dismayed fans at Old Trafford when he left United for Chelsea in the summer of 1995. "Sparky" has continued to deliver the goods at Stamford Bridge despite competition from Italians Gianluca Vialli and Gianfranco Zola. Muscular and stubborn on the pitch, quietly spoken and articulate off it. Played at Barcelona from 1986-88. Capped 60 times for Wales.

Gianfranco Zola (forward) 30. Diminutive Sardinian who has been spellbinding since his transfer from Parma late last year, ousting compatriot Gianluca Vialli up front. Lethal from free-kicks. His goal for Italy floored England at Wembley a week ago.

Gianluca Vialli (forward) 32. Joined within days of captaining Juventus to the European Cup last year. Lured to London on a free transfer by his old friend Gullit. Outspoken and principled, he has expressed his displeasure at spending so much time on the bench this season. May well be a substitute on Saturday but has the potential to wreak havoc if he comes on. Scored what turned out to be Chelsea's winner against United in the league clash at Old Trafford in November.
